headline: High: slim can read/write container artifacts and secrets while authelia exposes broad network/OAuth surfaces, creating default-path leakage and action-conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia has no documented shared channel to ingest slim output by default, and slim is an interactive CLI with stdin/stdout plus filesystem access. A prompt-injection path would require manual copy/paste or an added bridge, so the pathway exists but is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies slim stdout into authelia-managed input or config
IF a shared file or terminal transcript is used as an instruction channel
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate terminals and avoid copy-pasting outputs
Disable any workflow that feeds CLI output into auth policy text
Review pasted content before reusing it
Use read-only logs for slim output

B_data_leakage.rationale: Slim explicitly reads filesystem artifacts, certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, while authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC surfaces. If both touch the same workspace or secrets, slim can expose sensitive material that authelia could then transmit or act on. The interaction is plausible in default engineering workflows, though not proven shared by profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or secret store
IF slim reads certificate private keys or registry credentials from files authelia can reach
IF authelia forwards those values through OIDC/ForwardAuth flows
mitigations: Separate workspaces and secret mounts
Rotate any credentials exposed to slim
Restrict authelia egress to required IdP endpoints
Run slim against sanitized copies of images and files
Audit logs for secret-bearing output

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia is not documented as writing the filesystem, while slim can write files and execute shell commands. There is no evidence of shared mutable state or locking, so direct write-write conflict is not established. The main overlap is operational rather than concurrent state corruption.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF slim writes generated artifacts that authelia later consumes
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Mount authelia inputs read-only
Disable unnecessary write paths in slim runs
Use per-agent service accounts
Check for file clobbering after each run

D_cascading_error.rationale: Slim can emit analysis results from container images and filesystem artifacts, and authelia can consume API/OIDC-facing outputs. If an operator or workflow treats slim's findings as authoritative without verification, authelia may propagate incorrect identity or policy decisions. The pairwise handoff is plausible, but the profiles do not show an automated trust chain, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF authelia consumes slim output as policy input without validation
IF slim reports container facts that are later used to configure auth rules
mitigations: Require human review before applying slim-derived changes
Validate slim outputs against a second source
Keep generated recommendations separate from enforced policy
Log provenance for any imported findings

E_compliance.rationale: Slim handles certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, while authelia is an authentication component with broad network egress. If regulated secrets or identity data are processed together, retention and residency controls can diverge across the pair. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a compliance-risk warning rather than a breach claim.
conditions: IF regulated identity data or secrets are processed by both agents
IF logs or artifacts from slim are retained longer than authelia policy allows
mitigations: Classify and minimize secret-bearing inputs
Set short log retention for both tools
Store outputs in a compliant region
Document which data classes each agent may touch
Purge temporary artifacts after each run
